CORRECTION_2026-08-04_venue_was_wrong.what_was_wrong: The 2026-08-03 pass named fcn.80051b84 'the results-screen token renderer' and claimed the masked unlock bit 'selects earned-vs-locked presentation (the real icon versus the red ?)'. I read three near-identical mask-and-call blocks, matched them to the three results-screen token icons I had seen in C04's screenshots, and never disassembled the callee or checked the caller.
CORRECTION_2026-08-04_venue_was_wrong.what_it_actually_is: An IN-WORLD per-frame marker stage. Its ONLY caller is the gameplay state machine 0x8004ECD4. Its first half is gated on live player fields (0x800A659E==0x0B, 0x800A657C==0) and draws at Flik's live world position 0x800A6500/04/08. Its second half walks the three reward-token records and calls the marker stage 0x80051938 with (record, sprite_id, unlock_bit).
CORRECTION_2026-08-04_venue_was_wrong.what_the_bit_actually_does: 0x80051938 falls through into 0x80051940: reads record[0]/[4]/[8] as world X/Y/Z, takes the squared distance to the eye position 0x8009EC50/54/58 with each delta >>8, and RETURNS if that exceeds 0x0004C8FF (a distance cull). Then 'beqz a2' sets a2=0x60 when the bit is SET and leaves a2=0 when CLEAR; v0 = 0x60 - a2. The pair (0xC0, v0) is therefore (0xC0,0x00) set and (0xC0,0x60) clear -- a COLOUR/TINT component pair passed to the same sprite draw 0x80022FE0 the first half uses, at record Y - 0x1A00 (hoisted above the object). The record is then registered into a marker list at 0x800B1B58 + i*16 with a count at 0x800824CA capped at 0x2F. The bit modulates an in-world marker's TINT. There is no '?' sprite anywhere in this path.
CORRECTION_2026-08-04_venue_was_wrong.what_is_unchanged: The bit->record->sprite map is untouched and remains fully pinned: bit 0x01 = grain reward (record 0x80090B80, G_REWARD_SNAPSHOT, sprite 0x28); bit 0x02 = FLIK letters (record 0x800B3988, G_FLK_SNAPSHOT, sprite 0x1F); bit 0x04 = ENEMIES (record 0x80090B68, all-defeated event object, sprite 0x1B). The array (0x8009B878), the index (0x8008245C), the consumed sentinel 0x80000000, and 0x01|0x02|0x04 == 7 are all unchanged. C17's 'which bit is which axis' hedge is still closed, and the third-axis correction (enemies, NOT seeds) still stands -- each axis's own reward record is passed with exactly one bit, which is a direct pinned association independent of venue.
CORRECTION_2026-08-04_venue_was_wrong.how_it_was_caught: While scoping follow-up work I listed the neighbouring functions in analysis/functions.json and saw the census name fcn.80051b84 'effect_render_stage', sitting between effect_drop_spawn_stage and the harvester update. That prompted a caller check (only 0x8004ECD4, the gameplay state machine) and a read of the callee, which settled it.
CORRECTION_2026-08-04_venue_was_wrong.lesson: I inferred the VENUE from a visual match (three blocks <-> three on-screen icons) instead of reading the caller and the callee. Instruction pins prove what an instruction IS, not what the surrounding function is FOR; a pin tool that verifies 25/25 words can still sit under a wrong narrative. Cheap guards that would have caught it: check the caller set, and read the callee, before naming a function.

COUNTER_ANIMATION_CLOSED_2026-08-04.trigger: Operator: 'go for 1' -- decode the counter animation driver, the last undecoded piece of the results screen.
COUNTER_ANIMATION_CLOSED_2026-08-04.method: FULLY OFFLINE. With the load base 0x800B5788 established, tools/phase4_c05_counter_animation.c pins 46/46 instruction words directly against the pristine REBUILD/files/BITS/MEMORY.BIN. No emulator was used.
COUNTER_ANIMATION_CLOSED_2026-08-04.loop: The whole screen is one per-frame loop: 0x800B7F98 (jal wait_for_frame_sync_flag 0x8003F2F0) ... 0x800B8740 (bne s3, zero -> 0x800B7F98). s3 is the screen countdown, seeded to 800 at 0x800B7F20 and decremented once per frame while > 0.

three_numerators.enemies: s5, target [sp+0x50] = [0x80082258] - [0x800A658E] = TOTAL - REMAINING = DEFEATED, computed once up front at 0x800B7E34/4C/50

COUNTER_ANIMATION_CLOSED_2026-08-04.increment_law: All three identical: if (numerator < target && fp == 0) { numerator++; sfx id 14 via 0x800435F8 }. fp toggles every frame (fp = (fp+1) & 1 at 0x800B8614/1C), so THE COUNTERS ADVANCE ONE UNIT EVERY OTHER FRAME -- 30 Hz, not 60. s1 = (s1+1) & 0x0F on the fp==0 frames is the spinning-icon animation phase.
COUNTER_ANIMATION_CLOSED_2026-08-04.digit_rendering: hud_draw_sprite_tile(x, y, tile, GLYPH): tile 56 is the digit font and the FOURTH argument is the glyph index, with 10 = the '/' glyph. The tens digit is numerator/10 via the classic 0x66666667 magic-multiply reciprocal (0x800B7F8C/8024/803C); the units digit is numerator - tens*10.
COUNTER_ANIMATION_CLOSED_2026-08-04.grain_denominator_is_universal: Row 1 emits [tens][units] '/' then the LITERAL glyphs 5 and 0 (0x800B8090 a3=5, 0x800B80A4 a3=0). The denominator is two hardcoded digits in shared overlay code, so the grain requirement is 50 on EVERY level. This settles the question left open earlier on 2026-08-04; the only per-level number on the screen is the enemy total 0x80082258.
COUNTER_ANIMATION_CLOSED_2026-08-04.header_tile: 0x800B7FC0 reads the goal latch 0x800823A0: ==1 selects header tile 54, otherwise tile 55. So the banner itself is latch-driven.
COUNTER_ANIMATION_CLOSED_2026-08-04.skip_is_a_fast_forward_not_a_skip: A FRESH press on the face-button mask 0xF000 -- [0x80082412] & 0xF000 nonzero AND [0x800822E4] & 0xF000 zero, both zeroed at screen entry, i.e. an edge detector -- enters the finish block, but only inside the window 25 <= s3 < 740. If all three numerators are already at target and the one-shot flag [sp+0x58] is clear, s3 = 24 (end the screen shortly). OTHERWISE s3 = 54 AND the numerators are SNAPPED to their targets (0x800B8710/20/34). So pressing a button FAST-FORWARDS the count-up rather than skipping the screen -- which also explains how a token can appear immediately after a press: tokens are gated on the numerator reaching the total, and the snap satisfies that gate.
COUNTER_ANIMATION_CLOSED_2026-08-04.popcount_table: 0x800BE444 holds a 16-entry table whose disc bytes are exactly popcount(index) for 0..15 (0,1,1,2,1,2,2,3,1,2,2,3,2,3,3,4); the next byte is 252, i.e. only the 4-bit domain is meaningful -- matching the committed src_re/level_complete_results_800b7da0.c note that 'the retail table is only meaningful for reachable 4-bit masks'. It is also, with some irony, exactly what the auto-generated Canon page name 'popcount8' was describing. CAVEAT: this table lies in MEMORY.BIN's runtime-mutable tail (past +0x8112, the region that differed between disc and RAM), so these are the DISC bytes; a live re-read would be needed to prove the loaded copy is not rewritten. Flagged, not asserted.
COUNTER_ANIMATION_CLOSED_2026-08-04.corroborates_committed_source: src_re/level_complete_results_800b7da0.c independently records RESULT_COUNT_TARGET, the s6-vs-literal-4 medal compare, and the 0x800BE444 warning -- all consistent with this decode.
COUNTER_ANIMATION_CLOSED_2026-08-04.evidence: tools/phase4_c05_counter_animation.c (46/46 pins + the popcount table check), offline against BITS/MEMORY.BIN.

ITEM3_RESOLVED_2026-08-04_semitransparen.supersedes: ITEM3_MARKER_TINT_INCONCLUSIVE_2026-08-04. That block correctly retracted the 'tint' wording and correctly reported the A/B as inconclusive; it wrongly concluded no resident reader of the field existed. There IS one -- I had searched for the wrong displacement.
ITEM3_RESOLVED_2026-08-04_semitransparen.how_it_was_found: Rather than search for a literal displacement again, I enumerated who touches the record COUNT at 0x80082374 (gp+0x5DC). Exactly four functions do: the two producers (0x80022FE0, 0x80023544), a reset (0x800252A0), and ONE consumer, 0x80023ABC. That bounds the search completely instead of relying on a guessed offset.
ITEM3_RESOLVED_2026-08-04_semitransparen.why_the_first_search_missed_it: The record actually begins at 0x8009E8D0, not 0x8009E8E0. The producers address it as 0x800A0000-0x1720 + i*28 (so the bit-dependent field looks like '+0x02'), but the consumer sets t6 = 0x800A0000-0x1730 = 0x8009E8D0 and walks a POINTER t0 = t6 + 0x12 with a 28-byte stride. Same address, different base -- so grepping for the -0x171e displacement found nothing.
ITEM3_RESOLVED_2026-08-04_semitransparen.the_decision: Consumer at 0x80023C54: lh v1,(t0); li v0,0x60; beq v1,v0 -> skip; else prim = [0x8008249C]; prim[7] |= 0x02. The SAME record's +0x08/+0x09/+0x0A are written to prim[4]/prim[5]/prim[6], and a PS1 GPU packet's first word after the tag is 0xCC_BBGGRR -- so prim[4..6] are R,G,B and prim[7] is the COMMAND byte, whose bit 0x02 is the semi-transparency (ABE) flag. ORing 0x02 into it makes the primitive translucent.
ITEM3_RESOLVED_2026-08-04_semitransparen.RESULT: The field is a SEMI-TRANSPARENCY SELECTOR, not a colour/tint. Note the direction: bit CLEAR (axis NOT yet earned) -> value 0x60 -> equals 0x60 -> marker drawn OPAQUE; bit SET (axis ALREADY earned) -> value 0x00 -> not equal -> marker drawn SEMI-TRANSPARENT.
ITEM3_RESOLVED_2026-08-04_semitransparen.consistency: This is the same visual language as the results screen's already-earned token, reached by a different mechanism: the results screen modulates colour via 0x80026858 with (128,128,128), the in-world marker sets the GPU's ABE bit. Both say 'already earned' by making the thing see-through, which is a satisfying independent cross-check on the whole bit-map story.
ITEM3_RESOLVED_2026-08-04_semitransparen.evidence: tools/phase4_c05_marker_semitransparency.c -- 21/21 pins, first build, offline against the pristine EXE. The live A/B is no longer needed; it would only corroborate.
ITEM3_RESOLVED_2026-08-04_semitransparen.lesson: Three passes on one field: wrong venue, then wrong semantic, then 'unknown', then resolved. What finally worked was bounding the consumer set by an INVARIANT (who touches the count) instead of guessing an address form. When a displacement grep comes back empty, suspect the base, not the absence of a reader.
